intimacy.title: Intimacy
intimacy.intro: Ideas, a vibe, and a way to reach out. Nothing here is sent without you tapping send, and nothing is inferred from your cycle.

intimacy.libidoLowNote: Low desire is valid. Rest, warmth, and closeness without sex count too.
intimacy.libidoHighNote: Strong desire is welcome. Keep the pace yours and say what you enjoy.

intimacy.consentNote: Ideas are not consent. Anything shared happens only when both of you want it, and either of you can stop at any point.

cycleBasics.title: Cycle basics
cycleBasics.body: A cycle runs from the first day of one period to the first day of the next. Lengths vary, and many people have a cycle between about 21 and 40 days.

questions.q: What counts as day 1 of a cycle?
options: The first day of your period
The day you start a new check-in
questions.explain: Day 1 is the first day of bleeding. Counting from there keeps the rest simple.

questions.q: Why might a cycle be a little longer or shorter from month to month?
options: Stress, sleep, travel, and illness can all shift timing
questions.explain: Normal variation is common. Persistent big changes are a good reason to talk to a clinician.

whatIsNormal.title: What is normal?
whatIsNormal.body: Normal varies a lot. Cramps, flow, and mood can change with age, stress, and health. Tracking helps you notice what is usual for you.

questions.q: Which is a good reason to see a clinician?
options: Your period is a day shorter than last month
Bleeding that soaks a pad every hour or lasts much longer than usual
questions.explain: Heavy or prolonged bleeding, severe pain, or fever deserve a professional look, even if it is the first time.

questions.q: What is the most useful thing to track?
options: What feels usual for you, over a few months
Nothing, because patterns do not matter
questions.explain: Patterns over several months matter more than any single day.

talkingToClinician.title: Talking to a clinician
talkingToClinician.body: Bring a short summary: when your cycle started, what changed, and what worries you. Writing it down before the visit helps.

questions.q: What helps most before a clinic visit?
options: A short note with dates and what changed
A list of other people's symptoms
questions.explain: A few dates and specific changes help a clinician help you quickly.

questions.q: If a question feels embarrassing, what is best?
options: Ask it anyway; clinicians hear it all the time
questions.explain: Clinicians expect these questions. Asking is the point of the visit.
